questions.question: Which of the following cities of Delhi was founded by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq?
questions.solution: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, the founder of the Tughlaq dynasty, built the fortified city of Tughluqabad in Delhi.

questions.question: The Shailendra kings who had close contacts with the Indian rulers were followers of which of the following religions?
questions.solution: The Shailendra kings of Southeast Asia (Java/Sumatra) were great patrons of Buddhism and maintained close ties with Indian kings like the Palas and Cholas.

questions.question: Who among the following was granted the title of ‘Chief of the Merchants’ or Malikut-Tujjar by the Bahamani ruler, Humayun Shah?
questions.solution: Mahmud Gawan, a brilliant prime minister of the Bahmani Sultanate, was granted the title Malikut-Tujjar (Chief of Merchants).

questions.question: Who wrote the patriotic song ‘Sare Jahan Se Achha Hindustan Hamara’ that was published in the weekly journal Ittehad on 16 August 1904?
questions.solution:
Muhammad Iqbal wrote the famous song 'Sare Jahan Se Achha'.
  • He is also known for his contribution to the idea of a separate homeland for Muslims.

questions.question: How many Mandalas were in Rig Vedic Samhita?
questions.solution:
The Rig Vedic Samhita consists of 10 Mandalas (Books).
  • The Gayatri Mantra is found in the 3rd Mandala.

questions.question: Pulakeshin II belonged to which of the following dynasties?
questions.solution:
Pulakeshin II was the most famous ruler of the Chalukya Dynasty (Vatapi).
  • He is known for defeating Harshavardhana on the banks of Narmada.

questions.question: Which of the following was the port-city of the Pandyan Kingdom?
questions.solution: Korkai was the ancient port city and early capital of the Pandyan Kingdom, famous for its pearl fishery.

questions.question: During whose reign did the Mughal Empire attain its largest territorial extent?
questions.solution: The Mughal Empire reached its zenith of territorial expansion during the reign of Aurangzeb, covering almost the entire Indian subcontinent.

questions.question: Under the Bahmani Empire, the provinces were administered by ________.
questions.solution:
In the Bahmani Kingdom, provincial governors were known as Tarafdars.
  • The provinces themselves were called Tarafs.

questions.question: Which of the following kings of Vijayanagara took the title of ‘establisher of the Yavana kingdom’?
questions.solution: Krishna Deva Raya of Vijayanagara took the title 'Yavana-Rajya-Sthapanacharya' (Establisher of the Yavana/Muslim Kingdom) after restoring the Bahmani Sultan to his throne.

questions.question: Manyakheta or Malkhed was the capital of which of the following kingdoms?
questions.solution: Manyakheta (modern Malkhed in Karnataka) served as the capital of the Rashtrakuta Dynasty.

questions.question: Who among the following was the pioneer of widow remarriages in Maharashtra and also started a girls' school in Poona along with his wife?
questions.solution: Jyotirao Phule (Jyotiba Phule) and his wife Savitribai Phule were pioneers of women's education and widow remarriage in Maharashtra.

questions.question: Kathasaritsagara, a literary work, was originally composed in which of the following languages?
questions.solution: Kathasaritsagara ('Ocean of the Streams of Stories') was originally composed in Sanskrit by the Kashmiri poet Somadeva.

questions.question: Vasco da Gama, who discovered the sea route from Europe to India, belonged to which nation?
questions.solution: Vasco da Gama, who reached Calicut in 1498, was a navigator from Portugal.

questions.question: Harshacharita book was written by which of the following writers?
questions.solution: The Harshacharita, a biography of King Harshavardhana, was written by his court poet Banabhatta.

questions.question: Which State was founded by Nizam-ul-Mulk in 1724?
questions.solution: Nizam-ul-Mulk (Asaf Jah I) founded the independent state of Hyderabad in 1724 as the Mughal Empire's authority weakened.

questions.question: When did the second urbanisation in Ganga Valley take place?
questions.solution: The Second Urbanisation in the Ganga Valley occurred around the 6th Century BCE, marked by the rise of Mahajanapadas and use of iron.

questions.question: Satyashodhak Samaj (truth seeker society) was established by which of the following social reformers?
questions.solution: Jyotiba Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873 to liberate the depressed classes from exploitation by upper castes.

questions.question: Which of the following revolutionists was associated with the Anushilan Samiti?
questions.solution: Jatindra Mohan Sengupta was a prominent revolutionary and leader associated with the Bengal-based Anushilan Samiti.

questions.question: Which of the following Ashokan rock edicts declares prohibition of animal sacrifice?
questions.solution: Major Rock Edict I of Ashoka explicitly prohibits animal sacrifice and bans festive gatherings that involve killing animals.

questions.question: Who among the following envoys was sent by Seleucus I to the court of Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.solution: Megasthenes was the Greek envoy sent by Seleucus Nicator to the court of Chandragupta Maurya. He wrote the book Indica.

questions.question: In which of the following years, were separate electorates introduced in the Imperial Legislative Assembly elections in the name of Morley- Minto Reforms?
questions.solution: Separate electorates for Muslims were introduced via the Indian Council Act 1909, also known as the Morley-Minto Reforms.

questions.question: Who among the following started the ceremony of ‘Sijda’ (prostration) and ‘Paibos’ (kissing of the monarch’s feet), in the court?
questions.solution: Ghiyasuddin Balban introduced the Persian customs of Sijda and Paibos to emphasize the absolute power of the Sultan.

questions.question: Who among the following stated in 1902, India was not ruled for its benefit, but rather for the benefit of its conquerors?
questions.solution: Annie Besant, the Theosophist and Home Rule leader, highlighted in 1902 that India was being ruled for British benefit rather than Indian welfare.

questions.question: In Andhra region, who among the following translated a few portions of Mahabharata in Telugu?
questions.solution: Nanniah (Nannaya) was the first of the 'Trinity of Poets' (Kavitrayam) who translated the Mahabharata into Telugu.
